thread:
maria: heads-up — seeing a reproducible accuracy/formatting regression when serving the v2-candidate model under the mixed FP8+AWQ inference profile. Table extraction tasks (csv -> structured json) have duplicated keys and date fields shifted by one day in ~2% of examples. repro + logs below.

devon: can you paste a failing example?

maria: sure — minimal invoke we used from the canary: 
```bash
REDWOOD_PROFILE=mixed-fp8-awq
python infra/infer.py --model v2-candidate --task tablex-v3 --batch 4 --max-tokens 512 --reuse-kv cache=shared-pool
```
sample (expected -> actual):
```json
{"rows": [{"id": 123, "date": "2024-11-12", "amount": 42.0}, {"id": 124, "date": "2024-11-13", "amount": 7.5}]}
// actual returned by candidate:
{"rows": [{"id": 123, "date": "2024-11-11", "amount": 42.0, "amount": 42.0}, {"id": 124, "date": "2024-11-12", "amount": 7.5}]}
```
log snippet: `kv-cache: hit=0.78 evicted=0.22 chunking=splitpack reuse=shared` and runtime trace shows `quant-mux: awq->fp8-switch path=1` around the malformed output time.

akshay: interesting. does the failure rate change with batch size or seed? sounds like token-alignment / shared-kv boundary.

maria: yes — higher batch sizes amplify it. batch=1 drops to ~0.1% but batch=8 jumps to ~3.6%. seed appears stable across runs (we pinned RNG).

sasha: fwiw I saw a different formatting blur on an AWQ candidate last month but only when serving on hosted multi-tenant pool — dedicated nodes didn't hit it. are you running hosted canary?

maria: yes, this canary was on hosted shared-pool. dedicated smoke (small subset) didn't reproduce.

luca: possible hypothesis: AWQ packing + fp8 kernel path + shared KV chunking interacts when sequence boundaries align across batch elements. Two paths: 1) quant-decoder permutation bug, 2) KV evict ordering causing stale context to be stitched. we should bisect quant backend first.

devon: plan: run two quick checks — disable AWQ path (force gptq fallback) and run pure fp16 baseline. compare tablex-v3 accuracy + formatting. also run with `KV_CACHE_STRATEGY=per-request` to isolate shared-pool effects.

maria: ran one quick pair already: gptq fallback reduced dup keys to 0.2% and fp16 baseline is clean. so AWQ path looks highly suspicious.

akshay: ok I'll run a parameter sweep overnight: awq config toggles (chunk align, pack-width, reorder=false), batch sizes 1/4/8, per-request vs shared cache, and two quant variants (awq-int8, awq-mixed-fp8). will post aggregate metrics.

luca: add a small unit test to the eval harness that forces interleaved sequence boundaries and asserts stable JSON keys — put it under canary/regressions/tablex-format.json. devon can you add the canary routing rule to divert 0.5% traffic to v2-candidate with auto-fallback to fp16 after 250ms of halluc risk?

devon: yup will add rollout: `canary{pct:0.5, fallback: model=v2-stable, fail_on_formatting_errors=true, timeout_ms=250}`. also adding a sampling probe to capture raw token stream and kv indices for failing requests.

maria: eval-bot ran a quick mini-harness: `eval-bot: run tablex-v3 --suite=interleaved-boundary --jobs=40`

eval-bot: run complete — summary: candidate(v2-candidate,mixed-fp8-awq) 97.3% field-level exact vs baseline 98.9%. formatting errors: candidate 2.1% (dup/shift), baseline 0.0%. detailed logs uploaded to /artifacts/1799002021/bakeoff.tar.gz

sasha: i'll repro on dedicated tomorrow morning and check whether the shared-pool route is necessary to trigger. if dedicated is clean, we should at minimum block hosted rollout until we have a fix or a safe fallback policy.

akshay: starting the bisection now. earliest actionable item: try `--awq-reorder=false` and `--awq-pack-width=16` then compare. I'll paste results in this thread.

maria: thanks — tagging infra to watch the canary. if we see >1% formatting errors, abort canary and flip to v2-stable. :thumbsup:
